formulaIdentity.productName: Cantu Shea Butter Cleansing Cream Shampoo
formulaIdentity.fingerprintMethod: sha256 of packet canonicalInci joined with ', '
formulaIdentity.sourceTier: frozen packet canonical INCI; positioning: retailer + manufacturer
formulaIdentity.conflictNotes: Manufacturer page disclaimer ('ingredient list ... may vary from what's on the product packaging') is a generic disclaimer, not a conflict (ID-3); recorded, no confidence effect. 'Shea butter' maps to Butyrospermum Parkii Butter (10); 'Vitamin B complex' to Panthenol (14). Manufacturer claims are in English on the manufacturer source.

cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate by C1: Sodium C14-16 Olefin Sulfonate (2, sulfonate type) buffered by prominent Cocamidopropyl Betaine (3); no reinforcing anionic. Cocamide DIPA (4) and PEG-150 Distearate (8) are not routes (C3); Steareth-4 and Polysorbate 20 are post-fragrance solubilizers. 'Removes buildup'/'gentle' claims cannot move it (Section 4).

conditioningLevel.rationale: One meaningful system plus light routes: Acrylates Copolymer (6), Shea Butter (10, post-fragrance), Polyester-37 (11), Glycol Distearate (13), Panthenol (14), Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride (15), Polyquaternium-39 (19), Glycerin (5). C2 not met: no prominent silicone or prominent payload lipid. 'Cream'/'rich' wording does not raise it (C7, W-RICH). Counter-signal toward high: two cationic polymers + shea + film formers.

depositionLoad.rationale: Four families converge (film formers, waxy shea, two cationic polymers), but only Acrylates Copolymer is prominent and it often acts as a suspending polymer.

persistence.rationale: Waxy shea (6.4) and PQ-39/film formers can persist; all except acrylates are post-fragrance.

weightPotential.counterevidence: Late positions of shea (10), guar (15), PQ-39 (19) and the likely suspending role of Acrylates Copolymer argue toward low.
weightPotential.whyThisBand: Interacting light/moderate routes across four families plausibly leave a bounded residue under ordinary reset.
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: Not low (W2): four distinct families including waxy shea, two cationic polymers and film formers converge; calling it lightweight would understate residue risk. Not high: no silicone, shea not prominent (no W-RICH), reset not limited. 'Ohne zu beschweren' and 'rich creamy' claims do not move the band (6.5).
weightPotential.confidenceLimitingFactor: Function of Acrylates Copolymer/Polyester-37 (film vs. rheology) and low use levels could move it one band to low.

focusPrimary.counterSignal: Positioned as gentle, creamy, conditioning cleansing; moderate (not strong) cleansing; four deposition families.
focusPrimary.decisionTrace: Dominant positioning across name ('Cleansing Cream Shampoo'), manufacturer ('Rich creamy lather removes buildup', 'gently removes heavy build-up from the hair and scalp', moderate) and directions ('second lather ... for heavy product build up') is buildup removal -> clarifying candidate (7.1). F6 compatibility: cleansing moderate, conditioning moderate (not high), weight moderate (not high) -> compatible. Competing claims: 'protect against breakage' (repair verdict nonspecific: no protein/damage cluster) and 'nourish curls' (supporting). Route: AOS/betaine chassis (2, 3).
focusPrimary.rationale: clarifying by 7.1/7.2/F6: dominant buildup-removal positioning with a compatible formula; moderate because the product is also positioned as gentle/conditioning.

focusSecondary.decisionTrace: Empty default considered. moisture candidate ('to nourish curls and coils', retailer 'pflegt ... geschmeidig') has a plausible independent route (Glycerin 5, Panthenol 14, shea 10, polymers) but the wording is a supporting ingredient sentence rather than distinct product positioning; repair ('helps protect against breakage') has a nonspecific formula verdict. Neither meets all three Section 8 conditions with confidence.

usageRole.decisionTrace: Default regular. Losing trigger: U4 reset intent present ('removes buildup', manufacturer, moderate) but alternating requires cleansingStrength strong (moderate here). D1 false. No frequency or dandruff trigger.
usageRole.rationale: Regular: reset intent cannot fire alternating on a moderate formula (U4, Section 9).

scalpComfortTarget.rationale: No E2 sensitive/dry claim; 'milde Rezeptur', 'sanfte Reinigung ... von Haar und Kopfhaut' are mildness (SC1).

projection.thicknessRationale: T1 W moderate, C moderate: fine acceptable, normal ideal, coarse acceptable. Ordinary, no T6. T4: W neighbor low raises fine and keeps normal ideal; C neighbor high raises coarse -> no flag. 'Strukturiertes Haar'/curls wording ignored (T2).
projection.scalpTargetRationale: S-ORDINARY way 1: no qualifying E2 unit (buildup removal from the scalp is not an oily-scalp claim, E2); manufacturer source present -> high.
projection.cleansingIntensityRationale: I1: moderate -> regular (clarifying intensity needs strong cleansing). Matches normal bucket; I3 neighbor none.
projection.deepCleanserRationale: D1 false: 'Cleansing Cream Shampoo' and 'removes buildup' are not D1 stems; directions do not limit use to occasional resets. D2 not met; D3 not raised.

uncertainties: Whether buildup-removal positioning on a gentle, conditioning 'cleansing cream' makes clarifying the dominant focus or whether competing care claims make it general (7.2 'multiple claims').
6.3 lists acrylates copolymers as film_former, though in shampoos Acrylates Copolymer is often a suspending/rheology polymer.
S-FOCUS has no check for a clarifying focus with an ordinary target; none raised.
